shEntryLead.message: Type your shares one at a time, from the paper.

shEntryOtherSet.message: This share is from set $1. Type the shares of set $2.

shWrongCheck.message: This share has a typo. Compare it with the paper.

shLength.message: A share has 36 characters, in 9 groups of 4.

shNewer.message: This share was made by a newer Sixkey. Update Sixkey first.

shDifferentSets.message: These shares are from different sets.

shNoFit.message: These shares do not fit together. Check each one against its paper.

shStale.message: These shares rebuild a recovery key that does not open this vault. They may belong to an older recovery key, or to another Sixkey vault (set $1).

shIntro.message: Make $1 shares. Any $2 of them rebuild your recovery key; fewer reveal nothing. Keep them in different places.

shReplace.message: Make a new recovery key, shown only as shares (recommended)

shReplaceNote.message: Your current recovery key, and any shares of it, stop working once you finish. Until then nothing changes.

shSplitNote.message: Your current recovery key keeps working. The shares are one more way to it.

shWrongCode.message: That recovery key does not open this vault.

shCheckLead.message: Type the shares you have. Nothing is changed.

shCheckOk.message: These shares work: they rebuild the recovery key that opens your vault now.

shCheckRestart.message: The browser has not restarted since you switched to these shares. Check them once more after you restart it, and destroy the old recovery key only then.

shSwitchLost.message: If these are the shares you switched to last, that switch did not complete: your old recovery key still opens your vault. Keep it, and make the shares again.

shSaveWarn.message: A download folder that syncs (iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) puts the file in the cloud. Print it or move it to a USB stick, then delete it.

shKept.message: Share $1 is printed or written down

shNotYet.message: Nothing has changed yet: these shares open nothing until the check at the end.

shTestLead.message: Type shares $1 back from your paper, to be sure each was kept right.

shDone.message: Done. Any $1 of your $2 shares now rebuild your recovery key. Keep the old recovery key for now: after the next browser restart, use “Check my shares” once, and destroy the old key only when they pass.

shDoneSplit.message: Done. Any $1 of your $2 shares rebuild your recovery key. Your recovery key paper still works too.

shLost.message: Lost a share? Make new shares with “Make a new recovery key”: the old key and every old share then stop working.

shPaperAny.message: Any $1 of the $2 shares rebuild your recovery key.

shPaperWhere.message: Use it only in Sixkey, on its restore screen (I have shares instead). Sixkey never asks for a share by email, chat or phone. This is not a crypto-wallet phrase. Never photograph it.
